'''Shyam Swarup Agarwal''' (5 July 1941 – 2 December 2013) was an Indian geneticist, immunologist and the director of [[Sanjay Gandhi Postgraduate Institute of Medical Sciences]] (SGPGI-MS), Lucknow. A former director of the Advanced Center for Treatment, Research and Education in Cancer (ACTREC) at the [[Tata Memorial Centre]], he was the pioneer of medical genetics and clinical immunology education in India. Known for his researches in the fields of genetics and molecular biology, he was an Emeritus Professor of the [[National Academy of Medical Sciences]], and an elected fellow of all the three major Indian science academies, namely, the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]], [[National Academy of Sciences, India]], and the [[Indian National Science Academy]]. The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], the apex agency of the Government of India for scientific research, awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], one of the highest Indian science awards for his contributions to Medical Sciences in 1986.<ref name="View Bhatnagar Awardees">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/AwardeeList.aspx | title=View Bhatnagar Awardees | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | date=2016 | access-date=12 November 2016 | url-status=live | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161016194310/http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/AwardeeList.aspx | archive-date=16 October 2016 }}</ref>{{Refn|group=note|Long link - please select award year to see details}}

== Biography ==
[[File:Lucknowuniversity.jpg|thumb|left|235px|Lucknow University – Old campus]]

Shyam Swarup Agarwal was born on 5 July 1941 in [[Bareilly]], an industrial city in the Indian state of [[Uttar Pradesh]] to Shyam Dulari and Satya Swarup Agrawal.<ref name="Shyam Swarup Agarwal (1941–2013)">{{Cite web |url=http://www.currentscience.ac.in/Volumes/106/05/0758.pdf |title=Shyam Swarup Agarwal (1941–2013) |last=Nitya Anand |date=2014 |publisher=Current Science}}</ref> His undergraduate studies were at Caning College of [[Lucknow University]] and he completed the course in 1958. Subsequently, he pursued a medical profession after earning an honors degree of MBBS from King George’s Medical College (present-day [[King George's Medical University]]) in 1963, passing the examination winning the Chancellor's Gold Medal for Best Student and the Hewitt Gold Medal for securing first rank.<ref name="Deceased fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://insaindia.res.in/detail/N95-1168 |title=Deceased fellow |date=2016 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171208003210/http://insaindia.res.in/detail/N95-1168 |archive-date=8 December 2017 }}</ref> He continued at KGMU for his MD which he completed in 1967 and moved to the US for his post-doctoral studies on an [[International Agency for Research on Cancer]] fellowship where he worked at the laboratory of [[Baruch Samuel Blumberg]] at [[Fox Chase Cancer Center]].{{Refn|group=note|[[Baruch Samuel Blumberg]] won the [[Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine]] in 1976.}} On his return to India in 1970, he joined his alma mater, KGMU, as a lecturer and served the institution till 1986 during which time he secured an FRCS from the [[Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada]] in 1976.<ref name="Expert Profile">{{Cite web |url=http://doctor.ndtv.com/expert/ndtv/expertid/112/Dr_SS_Agarwal.html |title=Expert Profile |date=2017 |publisher=ND TV |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170303042605/http://doctor.ndtv.com/expert/ndtv/expertid/112/Dr_SS_Agarwal.html |archive-date=3 March 2017 }}</ref> In 1986, he was invited by [[Sanjay Gandhi Postgraduate Institute of Medical Sciences]] (SGPGI-MS) to establish a department for medical genetics and clinical immunology. He headed the department as a professor and served as its director during two terms, 1993–97 and 2000–01.<ref name="Obituary">{{Cite web |url=http://connection.ebscohost.com/c/obituaries/95115148/shyam-swarup-agarwal-1941-2013 |title=Obituary |date=2017 |publisher=EBSCO Host |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170303043631/http://connection.ebscohost.com/c/obituaries/95115148/shyam-swarup-agarwal-1941-2013 |archive-date=3 March 2017 }}</ref> He [[Pension|superannuated]] from regular service in 2001 but continued his work by joining [[Tata Memorial Centre]] as the director of the newly established [[Tata Memorial Centre#ACTREC|Advanced Center for Treatment, Research and Education in Cancer]] (ACTREC). After three years of service, he moved out of Tata Memorial Centre in 2004 and was appointed as an adviser at the [[Central Drug Research Institute]]. Simultaneously, he worked as an honorary director of Research and Academics at the Vivekanand Polyclinic and Institute of Medical Sciences and was a Senior Scientist of the [[Indian National Science Academy]] from 2006 onwards.<ref name="INSA Senior Scientist">{{Cite web |url=http://insaindia.res.in/name1.php |title=INSA Senior Scientist |date=2017 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170224131755/http://insaindia.res.in/name1.php |archive-date=24 February 2017 }}</ref> He was also associated with ''Future Earth'', a non-governmental organization creating ecological awareness among people<ref name="Dr. S.S. Agarwal (MD-Hons, FRCPC)">{{Cite web |url=http://futurearth.org/leadership.html |title=Dr. S.S. Agarwal (MD-Hons, FRCPC) |date=2017 |publisher=Future Earth |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160129035720/http://futurearth.org/leadership.html |archive-date=29 January 2016 }}</ref> and served as an independent director of [[Regency Hospital, Kanpur]].<ref name="24th Annual Report">{{Cite web |url=http://www.regencyhospital.in/pdf/Annual%20Report-2012-2013.pdf |title=24th Annual Report |date=2017 |publisher=Regency Hospital |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170303043603/http://www.regencyhospital.in/pdf/Annual%20Report-2012-2013.pdf |archive-date=3 March 2017 }}</ref>

Agarwal was married to Pramila Das, a pathologist by profession, and the couple had a daughter, Rama and a son, Rahul.{{Citation needed|date= August 2018}} Agarwal died in Lucknow of a heart attack on 2 December 2013, at the age of 72.<ref name="Deceased fellow" />

== Legacy ==
[[File:Bhopal-Union Carbide 2.jpg|thumb|235px|An image of [[Methyl isocyanate]] tanks at Union Carbide factory – 2008 photo]]
[[File:Ginsengpflanze.jpg|thumb|''[[Panax ginseng]]'']]

Agarwal's researches spanned the fields of medical genetics and molecular biology.<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{Cite web |url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/content/Detail.aspx?AID=380 |title=Brief Profile of the Awardee |date=2017 |publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170302194423/http://ssbprize.gov.in/content/Detail.aspx?AID=380 |archive-date=2 March 2017 }}</ref><ref name="Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners">{{cite web | url=http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | title=Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | date=1999 | url-status=live | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304043957/http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | archive-date=4 March 2016 }}</ref> His early studies during his days at [[Fox Chase Cancer Center]] were focused on [[DNA polymerase]] and its role in DNA synthesis which elucidated its stability and as well as the mechanism of DNA repair.<ref name="Shyam Swarup Agarwal (1941–2013)" /> In 1984, Agarwal and his colleagues conducted studies on ''[[Panax ginseng]]'' and their work discovered the [[immunomodulatory]] properties of the plant<ref name="Deceased fellow" /><ref name="Expert Profile" /> which they revealed in an article, ''Immunomodulatory activity of Panax ginseng extract'', published in [[Planta Medica]] journal in December, the same year.<ref name="Immunomodulatory activity of Panax ginseng extract">{{Cite journal |vauthors=Singh VK, Agarwal SS, Gupta BM |title=Immunomodulatory activity of Panax ginseng extract |journal=Planta Medica |date=December 1984 |volume=50 |issue=6 |pages=462–5 |doi=10.1055/s-2007-969773 |pmid=6531406|s2cid=31983884 }}</ref> Researches on the [[Epidemiology|seroepidemiology]] of [[malaria]],<ref name="Serology and seroepidemiology of malaria">{{Cite journal |vauthors=Das SK, Srivastava IK, Dutta GP, Agarwal SS |title=Serology and seroepidemiology of malaria |url=http://repository.ias.ac.in/76114/ |journal=Journal of Communicable Diseases |date=1985 |volume=17 |issue=Supp. 1 |pages=68–76 |pmid=3831070 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170303042931/http://repository.ias.ac.in/76114/ |archive-date=3 March 2017 }}</ref> childhood [[cirrhosis]] and its [[polygenic]] inheritance and antenatal screening for [[thalassemia]] incidence were some of the other studies undertaken by him.<ref name="Expert Profile" />

Under the aegis of the Department of Clinical Immunology of SGPGI-MS, he undertook several projects of the Indian Council of Medical Research which included a study of the genetic effects in the wake of the [[Bhopal disaster|Bhopal Gas Tragedy]] of December 1984<ref name="Directory of Emeritus Professors">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nams-india.in/docs_pdfs/directory%20of%20emer.pdf |title=Directory of Emeritus Professors |date=2017 |publisher=National Academy of Medical Sciences |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304065250/http://www.nams-india.in/docs_pdfs/directory%20of%20emer.pdf |archive-date=4 March 2016 }}</ref>{{Refn|group=note|Bhopal disaster is known to be the worst industrial tragedy and the estimated death toll is over 3000.<ref name=" Bhopal trial: Eight convicted over India gas disaster">{{Cite web |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/south_asia/8725140.stm |title=Bhopal trial: Eight convicted over India gas disaster |date=7 June 2010 |publisher=BBC News |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100701125838/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/south_asia/8725140.stm |archive-date=1 July 2010 }}</ref>}} and a study of [[Handigodu syndrome]] prevalent in some parts of [[Karnataka]] which he identified as autosomal-dominant [[Spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia congenita|spondylo-epiphyseal dysplasia]]. He also undertook a task for [[Central Drug Research Institute]] (CDRI) when the institute developed ''Guggulipid'',<ref name="Guggulipid">{{Cite web |url=http://www.webmd.com/vitamins-supplements/ingredientmono-591-guggul.aspx?activeingredientid=591 |title=Guggulipid |date=2017 |publisher=WebMed |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170302194041/http://www.webmd.com/vitamins-supplements/ingredientmono-591-guggul.aspx?activeingredientid=591 |archive-date=2 March 2017 }}</ref> a [[Lipid-lowering agent|hypolipideamic agent]] produced from the [[Ayurvedic]] drug, [[guggul]].<ref name="Clinical trial of ethyl acetate extract of gum gugulu (gugulipid) in primary hyperlipidemia">{{Cite journal |vauthors=Gopal K, Saran RK, Nityanand S, Gupta PP, Hasan M, Das SK, Sinha N, Agarwal SS |title=Clinical trial of ethyl acetate extract of gum gugulu (gugulipid) in primary hyperlipidemia |journal=J Assoc Physicians India |date=April 1986 |volume=34 |issue=4 |pages=249–51 |pmid=3531151 }}</ref><ref name="TylerPremila2012">{{cite book|author1=Virginia M Tyler|author2=M.S. Premila|title=Ayurvedic Herbs: A Clinical Guide to the Healing Plants of Traditional Indian Medicine|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=r7JmIeAw9JAC&pg=PA141|date=12 October 2012|publisher=Routledge|isbn=978-1-136-40511-2|pages=141–|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170302194513/https://books.google.com/books?id=r7JmIeAw9JAC&pg=PA141|archive-date=2 March 2017}}</ref><ref name="Pathak2009">{{cite book|author=Yashwant Vishnupant Pathak|title=Handbook of Nutraceuticals Volume I: Ingredients, Formulations, and Applications|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=dRa-TtRsXSkC&pg=PA203|date=24 November 2009|publisher=CRC Press|isbn=978-1-4200-8222-7|pages=203–|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170302202313/https://books.google.com/books?id=dRa-TtRsXSkC&pg=PA203|archive-date=2 March 2017}}</ref> He completed the clinical trials for the [[Phytopharmacology|phytopharmaceutical]] preparation which was subsequently cleared by the [[Drug Controller General of India]] for commercial marketing.<ref name="Therapeutic Effects of Guggul and Its Constituent Guggulsterone: Cardiovascular Benefits">{{Cite journal |last=Ruitang Deng |title=Therapeutic Effects of Guggul and Its Constituent Guggulsterone: Cardiovascular Benefits |journal=Cardiovascular Drug Reviews |date=2007 |volume=25 |issue=4 |pages=375–390 |doi=10.1111/j.1527-3466.2007.00023.x |pmid=18078436 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

His researches have been documented by way of several articles in peer-reviewed journals;<ref name="Agarwal SS [Author]">{{Cite journal |title=Agarwal SS [Author] |date=2017 |publisher=US National Library of Medicine |journal=List of Articles |volume = 24|issue = 20|pages = 1903–4|pmid = 20|last1 = Barthel|first1 = W.|last2 = Markwardt|first2 = F.|doi = 10.1016/0006-2952(75)90415-3}}</ref>{{Refn|group=note|Please see ''Selected bibliography'' section}} the online article repository of the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] has listed 171 of them.<ref name="Browse by Fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://repository.ias.ac.in/view/fellows/Agarwal=3AShyam_Swarup=3A=3A.html |title=Browse by Fellow |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170302193938/http://repository.ias.ac.in/view/fellows/Agarwal=3AShyam_Swarup=3A=3A.html |archive-date=2 March 2017 }}</ref> Besides, he has also contributed chapters to books published by others,<ref>{{cite book|title=Scientific Report – Institute for Cancer Research|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ruIgAQAAMAAJ|year=1976|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170302200619/https://books.google.com/books?id=ruIgAQAAMAAJ|archive-date=2 March 2017}}</ref> and his work has been cited by a number of authors and researchers.<ref name="BalickElisabetsky1996">{{cite book|author1=Michael J. Balick|author2=Elaine Elisabetsky|author3=Sarah A. Laird|title=Medicinal Resources of the Tropical Forest: Biodiversity and Its Importance to Human Health|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=eYu-AwAAQBAJ&pg=PA283|year=1996|publisher=Columbia University Press|isbn=978-0-231-10171-4|pages=283–|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170302202608/https://books.google.com/books?id=eYu-AwAAQBAJ&pg=PA283|archive-date=2 March 2017}}</ref> He also edited the Medical Genetics section of the ''API Textbook of Medicine'' (Ninth Edition, Two Volume Set) and wrote the introduction to the section.<ref name="MunjalSharm2012">{{cite book|author1=Y P Munjal|author2=Surendra K Sharm|title=API Textbook of Medicine, Ninth Edition, Two Volume Set|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=L7pW3yGjj7kC&pg=PA169|date=18 May 2012|publisher=JP Medical Ltd|isbn=978-93-5025-074-7|pages=169–|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170302202600/https://books.google.com/books?id=L7pW3yGjj7kC&pg=PA169|archive-date=2 March 2017}}</ref><ref name="Munjal2015">{{cite book|author=YP Munjal|title=API Textbook of Medicine (Volume I & II)|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=z39GCgAAQBAJ&pg=PA277|date=30 August 2015|publisher=JP Medical Ltd|isbn=978-93-5152-415-1|pages=277–|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170302194352/https://books.google.com/books?id=z39GCgAAQBAJ&pg=PA277|archive-date=2 March 2017}}</ref> On the academic front, he was a member of the expert panel set up by the Government of Uttar Pradesh for planning and establishment of [[Sanjay Gandhi Postgraduate Institute of Medical Sciences]] and when the institution was started in 1986, he became the founder head of the Department of Medical Genetics and Clinical Immunology.<ref name="Shyam Swarup Agarwal (1941–2013)" /> His contributions were reported in the introduction of the first DM post-graduate programme in medical genetics in India when the course was introduced at SGPGI-MS in 1990. He was responsible for the establishment of the Department of Clinical Immunology at the institution and was also credited with efforts in establishing a Medical Genetics Unit at KGMU.<ref name="Shyam Swarup Agarwal (1941–2013)" />

== Awards and honors ==
The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]] awarded him [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]], one of the highest Indian science awards in 1986;<ref name="Medical Sciences">{{Cite web |url=http://www.csir.res.in/external/heads/career/award/BPRIZE/Medical_SCIENCES.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130224074105/http://www.csir.res.in/External/Heads/career/award/BPRIZE/Medical_SCIENCES.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=24 February 2013 |title=Medical Sciences |date=2017 |publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research }}</ref> he received the Kamla Menon Research Award of the [[Indian Council of Medical Research]] the same year.<ref name="Expert Profile" /> The Government of Uttar Pradesh honored him with Vigyan Ratna Award in 2000.<ref name="Dr. S.S. Agarwal (MD-Hons, FRCPC)" /> In between, the Indian Academy of Sciences elected him as their fellow in 1985<ref name="Fellow profile">{{Cite web |url=http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Agarwal,_Prof._Shyam_Swarup |title=Fellow profile |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170302193939/http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Agarwal,_Prof._Shyam_Swarup |archive-date=2 March 2017 }}</ref> and he became an elected fellow of the Indian National Science Academy a decade later.<ref name="INSA Year Book 2016">{{Cite web |url=http://www.insaindia.res.in/pdf/YearBook_2016.pdf |title=INSA Year Book 2016 |date=2017 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161104001952/http://www.insaindia.res.in/pdf/YearBook_2016.pdf |archive-date=4 November 2016 }}</ref> A founder fellow of the Indian College of Physicians,<ref name="Founder Fellows of Indian College of Physicians">{{Cite web |url=http://www.icp-api.org/founder_fellows.html |title=Founder Fellows of Indian College of Physicians |date=2017 |publisher=Indian College of Physicians |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151117014846/http://www.icp-api.org/founder_fellows.html |archive-date=17 November 2015 }}</ref> he was an Emeritus Professor of the National Academy of Medical Sciences<ref name="Directory of Emeritus Professors" /> and an elected fellow of the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]].<ref name="Deceased Honorary Fellows, Foreign Fellows and Fellows - NASI">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nasi.org.in/deceased.htm |title=Deceased Honorary Fellows, Foreign Fellows and Fellows – NASI |date=2017 |publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150528102550/http://www.nasi.org.in/deceased.htm |archive-date=28 May 2015 }}</ref><ref name="NASI Year Book 2015">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nasi.org.in/Year%20Book%202015.pdf |title=NASI Year Book 2015 |date=2016 |publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150806211716/http://www.nasi.org.in/Year%20Book%202015.pdf |archive-date=6 August 2015 }}</ref> He was also a recipient of the Ranbaxy Research Award (1999)<ref name="Deceased fellow" /> and a life member of the Indian Institute of Immunology.<ref name="IIM Life Member">{{Cite web |url=http://indianimmunology.org/IISmembers.xls |title=IIM Life Member |date=2017 |publisher=Indian Institute of Immunology |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170303043315/http://indianimmunology.org/IISmembers.xls |archive-date=3 March 2017 }}</ref>

Agarwal delivered two award orations of the National Academy of Medical Sciences, namely, Glaxo Oration (1992) and Gen. Amir Chand Oration.<ref name="Deceased fellow" /> He also delivered two lectures of the Indian Society of Hematology and Blood Transfusion;<ref name="Shyam Swarup Agarwal (1941–2013)" /> J. B. Chatterjee Memorial Oration (1993) and J. B. Parekh Memorial Oration as well as two orations of the Indian National Science Academy, the Jawaharlal Nehru Birth Centenary Lecture of 2003<ref name="Jawaharlal Nehru Birth Centenary Lecture">{{Cite web |url=http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#jncl |title=Jawaharlal Nehru Birth Centenary Lecture |date=2017 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160916233840/http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#jncl |archive-date=16 September 2016 }}</ref> and the Dr, T. S. Tirumurti Memorial Lecture of 2005.<ref name="Dr TS Tirumurti Memorial Lecture">{{Cite web |url=http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#tstml |title=Dr TS Tirumurti Memorial Lecture |date=2017 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160916233840/http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#tstml |archive-date=16 September 2016 }}</ref> The other award orations delivered by him included Unichem lecture of the Association of Physicians of India (1979), M. P. Mehrotra Oration of the Association of Physicians of India, UP chapter (1981), Lajwanti Madan Oration of the Uttar Pradesh chapter of the [[Indian Medical Association]] (1985), C. R. Krishnamurthy Oration (1997), Mathur–Mehrotra Oration of [[Sarojini Naidu Medical College]] (1998) and Bhatia–Misra Oration of King George Medical University (2000).<ref name="Expert Profile" /> The Society for Indian Academy of Medical Genetics has instituted an annual award, ''Dr S S Agarwal Young Scientist Award'', in his honor, to recognize excellence in research in medical genetics among young researchers.<ref name="Dr S S Agarwal Young Scientist Award">{{Cite web |url=http://www.iamg.in/Dr_SS_Agarwal_Young_Scientist_Award.pdf |title=Dr S S Agarwal Young Scientist Award |date=2017 |publisher=Society for Indian Academy of Medical Genetics |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170302204255/http://www.iamg.in/Dr_SS_Agarwal_Young_Scientist_Award.pdf |archive-date=2 March 2017 }}</ref>
